title: Expand the cubic
text: Notice that the argument in the first logarithm is a perfect cube. You can apply the distribution repeatedly. \n $$\left(x-1\right)^2=x^2-2x+1$$ \n $$\left(x^2-2x+1\right) \left(x-1\right)=x^3-3x^2+x+\left(-x^2+2x-1\right)=x^3-3x^2+3x-1$$

title: Substitute the factored form
text: Substitute this factored form back into the expression: $$\log_2((x-1)**3)-\log_2(x-1)$$

title: Apply the law of logarithms for quotients
text: Use the law for quotients $$\log_b(a)-\log_b(c)=\log_b(a/c)$$ to combine the terms: $$\log_2\left(\frac{(x-1)**3}{x-1}\right)$$

title: Cancel common factors
text: Cancel the common factor of $$(x-1)$$ in the numerator and denominator to simplify the fraction: $$\log_2((x-1)**2).$$ Therefore, $$P(x)=\left(x-1\right)^2$$
